title: Chief Engineer Operations H/F
descriptionHtml:
📍 Paris / Île-de-France | Environnement Data Center | CDI | Périmètre multisite

Rejoignez mon client au cœur des infrastructures critiques.

Dans un contexte de forte croissance et de développement de ses infrastructures, mon client renforce son organisation Operations en France et crée un poste de Chief Engineer.

Au sein d'un nouvel pôle d'expertise technique transverse, vous devenez le référent technique des opérations sur plusieurs sites stratégiques en France, avec un périmètre prioritaire couvrant notamment deux sites.

Votre mission : apporter votre expertise, sécuriser les opérations et contribuer à faire progresser l'ensemble de l'organisation vers davantage de standardisation, de rigueur opérationnelle et d'excellence technique.

Ce poste s'adresse à un profil expérimenté qui souhaite aller au-delà de l'expertise technique pure et jouer un rôle central dans la structuration des opérations d'un acteur Data Center en pleine croissance.

Vos missions

Votre rôle

Le Chief Engineer intervient comme référent technique et opérationnel multisite.

Vous êtes à la fois :

  • un expert technique capable de challenger les équipes et les prestataires ;

  • un référent opérationnel garant de la sécurisation des opérations ;

  • un acteur transverse capable de fédérer des équipes aux profils et niveaux d'expérience différents.

Vous disposez d'une véritable autorité technique : lorsque les conditions de sécurité ou de maîtrise des risques ne sont pas réunies, vous êtes capable de challenger une opération et, si nécessaire, de prononcer un NO GO sur un mode opératoire ou une intervention.

Vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les responsables de site, qui conservent la responsabilité opérationnelle de leur périmètre.

Vos principales missions

1 - Être le référent technique des infrastructures critiques

Vous apportez votre expertise sur l'ensemble des infrastructures techniques du Data Center et êtes capable d'en comprendre les interactions et les impacts opérationnels.

Votre périmètre couvre notamment :

  • les infrastructures électriques HT/BT ;

  • les systèmes de secours électrique ;

  • les UPS / onduleurs ;

  • les groupes électrogènes ;

  • les infrastructures CVC / HVAC ;

  • les systèmes de refroidissement ;

  • la protection et la sécurité incendie ;

  • les systèmes de contrôle-commande et infrastructures associées.

Vous intervenez comme référent technique auprès des responsables de site et des équipes Operations, et êtes capable de challenger les différents interlocuteurs internes ou externes sur leurs choix et leurs pratiques.

2 - Sécuriser les opérations

L'une de vos responsabilités majeures sera de garantir que les opérations réalisées sur les infrastructures critiques sont préparées et exécutées dans les meilleures conditions de sécurité et de maîtrise des risques.

À ce titre, vous :

  • challengez les modes opératoires (MOP) ;

  • vérifiez la cohérence et l'exhaustivité des procédures ;

  • identifiez les risques et leurs impacts potentiels ;

  • sécurisez les opérations avant leur réalisation ;

  • challengez les premières analyses et propositions d'intervention ;

  • pouvez émettre un NO GO lorsqu'une opération ne présente pas les garanties nécessaires ;

  • accompagnez les responsables de site dans la prise de décision technique ;

  • contribuez à la mise en place de mécanismes de double vérification.

Vous êtes en quelque sorte le garde-fou technique de l'organisation, avec pour objectif de sécuriser les opérations sans perdre de vue les impératifs de continuité de service.

3- Structurer et harmoniser les pratiques

L'un des enjeux majeurs du poste est de contribuer à l'harmonisation des pratiques entre les différents sites.

Aujourd'hui, les niveaux de maturité et les pratiques peuvent varier d'un site à l'autre. Votre rôle sera de contribuer à construire un socle commun de méthodes et de standards opérationnels.

Vous serez notamment amené(e) à :

  • structurer les processus d'exploitation ;

  • définir et harmoniser les standards techniques ;

  • rédiger et améliorer les procédures et modes opératoires ;

  • mettre en place des workflows opérationnels ;

  • contrôler leur bonne application ;

  • identifier les écarts entre les sites ;

  • proposer et suivre les plans d'amélioration ;

  • partager les bonnes pratiques ;

  • réaliser des REX multisites ;

  • accompagner les équipes dans l'adoption des nouveaux standards.

La capacité à construire et faire vivre des process sera donc aussi importante que votre expertise technique.

4- Apporter votre expertise lors des incidents critiques

En cas d'incident technique complexe, vous intervenez comme référent technique auprès des équipes Facility et Operations.

Vous êtes notamment amené(e) à :

  • analyser techniquement l'incident ;

  • identifier les causes et les impacts potentiels ;

  • apporter votre expertise aux responsables de site ;

  • challenger les analyses proposées ;

  • accompagner les équipes internes et les prestataires ;

  • contribuer à la définition des actions correctives ;

  • participer à la résolution de l'incident ;

  • organiser et partager les retours d'expérience à l'échelle des différents sites.

Votre capacité à prendre du recul, analyser rapidement une situation complexe et apporter une réponse techniquement robuste sera essentielle.

5 - Développer une culture d'excellence opérationnelle

Vous ne vous contentez pas de définir les standards : vous accompagnez les équipes dans leur appropriation.

Vous serez ainsi amené(e) à :

  • former et accompagner les équipes ;

  • expliquer les exigences techniques et opérationnelles ;

  • faire progresser les pratiques ;

  • fédérer autour d'objectifs communs ;

  • accompagner la conduite du changement ;

  • favoriser le partage de connaissances entre les sites.

Vous disposez d'une forte capacité d'influence et savez faire avancer les sujets sans nécessairement disposer d'un lien hiérarchique direct.

6 - Être l'interlocuteur technique des clients majeurs

Vous serez capable de :

  • représenter la société sur les sujets techniques ;

  • expliquer une situation ou un incident complexe ;

  • présenter les actions mises en œuvre ;

  • répondre aux interrogations techniques des clients ;

  • apporter un discours structuré et crédible sur les enjeux d'exploitation et de sécurité des infrastructures.

Une organisation en construction

Vous rejoindrez un pôle d'expertise technique transverse nouvellement structuré, regroupant différentes compétences destinées à accompagner les opérations et les projets.

L'objectif est de créer une véritable communauté d'experts capable d'apporter son expertise à l'ensemble des sites et de faire progresser collectivement les standards d'exploitation.

Vous travaillerez au quotidien avec :

  • les responsables de site ;

  • les équipes Facility et Operations ;

  • les équipes projets ;

  • les experts techniques ;

  • les prestataires et partenaires externes ;

  • les fonctions transverses ;

Le poste est donc particulièrement transverse et nécessite une forte capacité à créer du lien entre les différentes parties prenantes.

Vos compétences

Votre profil

Vous disposez d'une expérience significative dans un environnement Data Center ou infrastructure critique fortement structurée.

Vous avez idéalement évolué dans un environnement où les exigences en matière de procédures, de sécurité opérationnelle, de maintenance et de continuité de service sont particulièrement élevées.

Une expérience dans un environnement critique comparable serait particulièrement appréciée.

Votre expertise technique

Vous disposez d'une excellente connaissance des infrastructures critiques et notamment :

descriptionHtml:
About AIOS

AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.

We’re at $450M ARR, growing from $7M/yr in April 2025. We’re faithfully serving >200k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’ve just launched Bolt Med, our international brand. We’re profitable.

Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

  1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.

  2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

  • Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.

  • Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026: Since April 2025 we've grown from 3k to 200k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.

  • Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.

  • Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2030: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.

  • Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here: Working at AIOS

Being a Clinical Pharmacist at AIOS

We are building a world-class team.

At AIOS Tech (Bolt Pharmacy), we're building the world's first full-stack AI doctor. Right now it's akin to assisted self-driving (and improving every day), so humans are prescribing with AI assisting their workflows.

You'll join our growing team of Independent Prescribers, working through GLP-1 weight-management consultations day in, day out. You understand that a great patient experience means catching everything you need to prescribe safely and confidently first time - not sending someone back and forth for information you should have picked up on intake.

You'll assess each patient on their own merits: the comorbidity, the interacting medication, the case that needs a second look, and make the right call. You’ll never compromise on safety or accuracy.

You'll:

  • Deliver safe, evidence-based GLP-1 prescribing for every patient on your list

  • Take full ownership of the clinical quality, safety and accuracy of your own consultations and records

  • Flag anything that needs escalating—a red flag, a near miss, a protocol gap—clearly and quickly

  • Follow, and help sharpen, our clinical protocols as they evolve

This role is suited to a confident, forward-thinking prescriber with sound clinical judgement, excellent attention to detail, and a strong commitment to patient safety.

Great performance in this role means your patients are safe, your records hold up to audit, and you're working through a full, steady caseload without ever cutting corners. If you nail this role, you'll be a strong candidate for more senior clinical positions as we grow.

This is an ongoing contractor engagement - full-time (40h) preferred, part-time (20h+) available - fully remote/WFH or hybrid onsite in Blackburn.

You’ll report directly to your team lead.

You’ll also work most closely with:

  • Noozhat Patel (UK Clinical Operations Lead)

  • Mobeen Nawaz (Clinical Team Lead)

  • Adedayo Titiloye (Deputy Superintendent Pharmacist)

Key Responsibilities

  • Prescribing: Deliver safe, evidence-based GLP-1 prescribing for every patient you see — assessing suitability, comorbidities and contraindications before you write anything.

  • Consultations: Run detailed, efficient consultations that capture everything you need the first time, so patients aren't stuck in back-and-forth messiness.

  • Monitoring: Track treatment response and side effects across your caseload, and adjust care promptly and safely.

  • Escalation: Recognise what's outside your remit, and escalate red flags, near misses or complex cases to your Senior Clinician Team Lead quickly and clearly.

  • Documentation: Keep accurate, concise and contemporaneous clinical records that hold up to audit.

  • Governance: Contribute to clinical audits, incident learning and quality improvement when asked.

  • Collaboration: Work smoothly with customer support, operational and technology teams to keep the service safe and moving in service of our patient base.

Need to Have

  • Registration: GPhC-registered pharmacist with an Independent Prescriber (IP) annotation, held for at least 1 year.

  • GLP-1 Confidence: You've prescribed weight-management, GLP-1s or a closely related area — comorbidities and polypharmacy don't throw you off protocol.

  • Clinical Reasoning: You think clearly and quickly within a protocol-led service.

  • Safety Mindset: Patient safety and quality are non-negotiable for you. Red flags don't get past you.

  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication, including confident patient counselling.

  • Pace: Comfortable in a fast-paced, high-volume, protocol-led environment, and you don't let volume compromise accuracy.

  • Digital Literacy: Confident using electronic health records and remote consultation platforms.

  • Flexibility: Willing to support evening or weekend rotas when needed. With sufficient notice, you work the hours that our patients need you to work so they can be served without long wait times and unnecessary friction.

Nice to Have

  • Consultation Modes: Experience with asynchronous, telephone and/or video consultations.

  • Specialist Training: Additional training in obesity or weight management, such as SCOPE certification.

  • Postgraduate: A postgraduate clinical diploma or equivalent.

  • Complex Patients: Comfortable managing patients with diabetes, cardiovascular disease, renal impairment or polypharmacy.

  • Governance Experience: Some experience contributing to clinical audits, incident investigations or quality-improvement projects.

  • Protocols: Exposure to developing SOPs, clinical protocols or prescribing pathways.

  • Startup Pace: Experience working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, ideally in the weight loss space.

  • Growth Mindset: An interest in eventually mentoring or supporting more junior colleagues as you grow with us.

  • Systems: Familiarity with clinical support and customer management systems.

Training and onboarding

  • Training is delivered completely remotely

Compensation & Benefits

You get paid above market salary and you get early stage equity, so you get really rich if we nail this.

title: Cloud Architect
descriptionHtml:
About Vitestro

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™). This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

We are looking for a Cloud Architect to shape and implement Vitestro's cloud platform with a clear, pragmatic technical direction. Our infrastructure runs on AWS and supports mission-critical, regulated medical device software. Vitestro is also realizing its first integration with Laboratory Information System (LIS) over the cloud, and delivering that connection is a core part of this role. We need someone who translates real operational and business constraints into working systems — someone whose first instinct is "what does this actually need to do, reliably and affordably," not "what's the most sophisticated way to solve this."

You will join the Platform & Connectivity team and build alongside its cloud, backend, and DevOps engineers. This is an individual-contributor technical leadership role, not a people-management position — you carry the architectural vision and build it hands-on with the team, rather than designing something for others to execute.

If you'd rather ship a solid, working solution than iterate endlessly toward a theoretically ideal one, and you have a track record of keeping cloud costs under control at scale, you'll thrive in this role.

First months at Vitestro

In your first months, you get to know our cloud platform, the device connectivity and the team. You review the current architecture, its costs and its production-readiness, and identify where the biggest risks and quick wins are. You take ownership of the cloud architecture for our first LIS integration, and you agree with the team on the first architectural standards for observability, logging and infrastructure as code.

This is what success looks like:

After 12 months, our first LIS integration runs reliably in production, with monitoring, alerting and failure handling in place. Cloud costs are predictable and under control, and key architectural decisions and trade-offs are recorded. The team uses shared patterns instead of reinventing solutions, and is confident running production systems as we move from pre-market to post-market.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Set the technical direction for our AWS-based cloud platform and build it hands-on with the team — weighing cost, operability, and production-readiness as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts

  • Own the cloud architecture of Vitestro's first LIS integration over the cloud: secure, reliable, and traceable data exchange between our platform and the hospital laboratory

  • Choose solutions on their merits rather than defaulting to the most AWS-native option — including other clouds, self-hosted tooling, or dedicated infrastructure when that's genuinely the better fit

  • Take implementations from a working prototype to something that's production-ready — monitoring, alerting, and failure handling included. You bring experience with production systems and advise the team on how to navigate from pre-market to post-market stages.

  • Establish architectural standards and patterns so similar problems (e.g. observability, logging, data pipelines) get solved consistently instead of reinvented each time

  • Keep cloud costs in check as part of everyday engineering decisions, catching expensive mistakes before they show up on an invoice

  • Balance short-term solutions driven by business needs and deadlines against the long-term architecture: make each trade-off explicit, record it, and plan the path from the tactical fix to the durable solution

  • Diagnose and resolve production issues across the cloud platform from logs, metrics, and traces


What You’ll Bring:

  • Deep, hands-on production experience with AWS at scale — not certification-level familiarity, but real experience with what breaks and what gets expensive as usage grows

  • Proven experience running production systems end to end, from design and release through monitoring and incident response, and the ability to advise a team that is new to production

  • Genuine experience building outside an AWS-only mindset — another cloud, self-hosted/open-source alternatives, or dedicated/on-premise infrastructure — enough to make an informed trade-off, not just AWS as the only tool you reach for

  • A track record of finishing what others started: turning a partial or unstable implementation into something genuinely reliable in production

  • Strong Infrastructure as Code practice (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, or AWS CDK) as the authoritative source of environment configuration

  • Comfortable operating in a regulated, security-conscious environment where architecture decisions have compliance implications

  • Familiarity with AWS cost structure, along with the ability to factor in cost-related considerations when designing infrastructure

  • Professional English; Dutch is a plus

Nice to have:

  • Experience specifically with observability/logging platforms at scale (e.g. OpenSearch, Grafana/Loki stacks, or equivalent) — bringing an implementation to production-hardened state, not just standing it up

  • Experience in medical device, healthcare, or another regulated industry

  • Familiarity with multi-tenant, per-customer cloud architectures (e.g. isolated accounts or workloads per client/region)

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

How We Work

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

  • We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

  • We focus on execution and delivering results.

  • We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

  • We challenge ideas, not people.

  • We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

  • We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary including a pension plan

  • 25 days of annual leave (full-time position)

  • A high-skilled team based in Utrecht

  • Frequent out-of-work team activities and an annual company weekend away

  • A training budget

  • The chance to help shape the new niche of autonomous medical robotics

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it.

Are you excited?

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you!

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. We would love to learn about your interest and experience and consider if you can be a good fit for Vitestro. Nobody is a perfect fit, and we welcome applications with imperfections. We offer a learning environment where we grow together!

title: Commercial Analytics Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Octopus Energy for Business

Octopus Energy for Business (OEB) is a rapidly scaling energy supplier with more than 130k business customers. We aim to accelerate the business sector’s transition to net zero whilst providing low-cost energy that meets the needs of our customers.

We’ve pioneered PPA-backed supply for mid-market businesses through Electric Match, led the way for SME smart tariffs with Shape Shifters and are the established market leader for enabling EV public charging through energy supply and services.

About the role

We’re seeking a highly skilled and data-driven Commercial Analytics Manager to modernise how we track and forecast our financial performance. In this role, you’ll take ownership of our business forecasting processes and lead the transition away from legacy, multi-tab spreadsheets. By leveraging modern data tools, you will build robust, automated pipelines to analyse margins, investigate variances, and provide actionable insights that optimise OEB's financial performance. You’ll collaborate closely with our Data team, finance teams, and senior leadership to ensure our financial strategies align with the company's sustainable growth objectives.


What you'll do

  • Provide consistent portfolio level reporting for OEB to determine overall net margins. This will include revenue, cost of sales, debt and operational expenditure.

  • Lead the development and management of the company’s forecast, ensuring accuracy and alignment with strategic goals.

  • Work with the team to interrogate the entire cost stack to influence pricing decisions.

  • Develop margin optimisation strategies, including pricing adjustments, cost reductions, and process improvements.

  • Improve accuracy of gross margin calculations in partnership with Finance and Pricing teams.

  • Lead meetings with colleagues and senior management to provide clear options in the decision making process.

  • Work closely with the pricing team to influence key decisions to ensure we provide customers with a wide range of tariffs which are set with a conscious view of outturned margins.

  • Provide monthly reporting packs to monitor different aspects of performance including budgets and variance analysis.

  • Work closely with business units to gather key inputs and assumptions for accurate forecasting.

  • Improve the tools behind our forecasting, moving away from spreadsheet-heavy processes towards Python and SQL-based analysis.

  • Compare forecasts with monthly actuals and thoroughly investigate variances across the business's book.


    • What you'll need

  • Strong proficiency in SQL to extract, manipulate, and transform complex commercial data.

  • Experience using Python for data analysis, automation, or financial modeling.

  • A minimum of 3 years experience of using data and coding to solve commercial, pricing, or financial problems.

  • A proven track record of untangling complex, legacy spreadsheet processes and replacing them with streamlined, automated solutions.

  • Strong financial acumen, particularly with reporting margins, forecasting, and variance analysis.

  • The ability to bridge the gap between commercial finance and data analytics, summarising complex findings into clear narratives for senior, non-technical stakeholders.

  • A self-starter mentality with the confidence to take ownership of a growing area, solve complex problems, and constantly introduce new processes.

  • Ideally, previous financial, commercial, or pricing experience within the energy industry (considered a strong bonus, though we are open to exceptional data-driven candidates from other sectors).

title: Commercial Associate
descriptionHtml:
This role is based out of our London office 🇬🇧

We are an office-first company & believe great products are made when we are together.

 

About Stacks

Stacks is building an AI-native platform that reinvents how modern finance teams run the monthly close. The opportunity is massive: every growing company depends on accurate, timely financial data, yet most are still operating with tools and workflows built for a different era.

 

In just two years, we’ve grown from a team of 2 to 30+ and are on a rapid trajectory. We’ve raised a $23m Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and we were recently recognised as one of Harmonic’s Hottest Startups of 2026.

 

We’re already trusted by leading European scale-ups including Pleo, Freetrade, and Motorway. Our team is a blend of finance, product, and technical experts from top-tier companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, Mollie, and Bunq, united by the drive to create a game-changing solution.

 

We’re a team that is deeply customer-obsessed, plays to win, and isn’t afraid to take big, bold bets. We move fast, hold a high bar, and are committed to growing together as we scale.

 

About the Role

Stacks is looking for a fiercely ambitious, entrepreneurial, and commercially driven Business Development Representative / Commercial Associate to join as one of our initial GTM hires!

 

In this high-impact role, you’ll collaborate closely with our Sales team to create and execute our GTM strategy at Stacks. If you’re excited by the idea of limitless growth and fast-paced challenges, this is a unique opportunity to accelerate your career as you help shape the future of Stacks.

🧱 What You'll Do

  • Outbound Strategy: Run multi-channel campaigns across email, phone, and LinkedIn. You'll be writing, testing, and iterating constantly.

  • Discovery & Qualification: Hold sharp, insight-led conversations with finance leaders. Your consulting instincts for asking the right questions will show up here.

  • Product Mastery: Get deep on the close process fast, so you can speak credibly about debits, credits, reconciliations, and the pain of a 10-day close.

  • Cross-functional Partnership: Work directly with our Sales team to shape messaging and build a repeatable outbound motion.

  • Growth Path: Clear track to AE. This is the launchpad role. You're looking at an 8-12 month trajectory into a mid-market deal-making role.

 

🧩 What You Need

  • Hunger & Grit: You're competitive, coachable, and don't flinch at a cold call.

  • Meaningful ownership: Competitive equity in a company scaling rapidly towards $10m ARR, where your impact will directly shape the outcome.

  • High-calibre team: Collaborate with people from companies like Uber, Plaid, Miro, and Mollie.

title: Company Operations Lead
descriptionHtml:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

ElevenLabs moves fast - by design. We run lean, we bias toward action, and we trust our people to figure things out. That's how we've built world-leading AI products in three years with a fraction of the headcount of our peers. But speed at 200 people and speed at 1,000+ people are different challenges, and the systems, habits, and connective tissue that let a company move fast without breaking things don't build themselves.

As our Company Operations Lead, you'll own the infrastructure that lets ElevenLabs keep its velocity as it scales. Not by adding process for process's sake - but by building the right systems, in the right places, at the right time, so that the rest of the company can focus on what they do best. You'll establish the operating layer that keeps a 50-country, hybrid organization coherent; drive the strategic planning cadence that keeps leadership aligned; and deploy a lean team of strategic generalists against the company's most urgent cross-functional challenges.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Operating Cadence: Running the planning and alignment cycles that keep the company pointed in the right direction. This includes OKR planning, workforce, and headcount planning.

  • Operating System: Building and maintaining the infrastructure layer that lets the company move faster. Systems of record, org taxonomy and governance, and the knowledge management systems that ensure information flow effectively across our remote-first team.

  • AI Enablement & Agentification: Ensuring every team at ElevenLabs has the tools, access, and knowledge to work effectively with AI. You'll own the internal AI enablement framework - managing tool access and rollout, identifying where agents and automation can accelerate how functions operate, and building the learning opportunities and champions programmes that drive deep adoption. You'll work closely with Security, IT, and the Automations team to ensure what gets built is built right.

  • Operations Centre of Excellence: Defining what great operations looks like at ElevenLabs and embedding it across the company. You'll set the blueprint that makes operational excellence repeatable and deploy the team as embedded operators inside other functions, standing up best practices, up-skilling teams, and handing off cleanly once the work is done.

Requirements

We do not require formal experience, certifications, or degrees. We do require:

  • Proven experience building and leading a Strategy & Operations or BizOps function at a high-growth technology company - ideally through a meaningful scaling inflection (Series B–D trajectory or equivalent).

  • Track record of standing up functions and systems from scratch and handing them off, rather than owning a permanent queue.

  • Structured problem-solving background - strategy consulting, a BizOps or Chief of Staff seat with genuine strategic scope, or an operator role that required both systems-building and executive influence.

  • Strong AI and tooling fluency - you should be pushing the organisation on what's possible with AI enablement, not chasing it.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management: you can partner with founders and Leads and earn trust quickly in a flat, high-velocity environment.

Bonus:

  • Experience inside a company that scaled through a 200 → 2,000+ person inflection.

  • Background that spans both consulting and operator roles - you've done the thinking and the building.

  • Familiarity with knowledge management, AI agentification, or internal tooling as an operational discipline.

Location

This role is remote. London or New York preferred.

title: Creative Director (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über Teaching Socials

Teaching Socials ist die führende Unternehmensberatung für Personal Brands im Finanz- & Immobilienbereich im DACH-Raum. Unser Team aus 25 High-Performern hat innerhalb von 2 Jahren ein konstantes Monatswachstum von über 750.000 € aufgebaut. Wir verbinden Sichtbarkeit, Kundenakquise und Unternehmenswachstum in einem System – und du sorgst mit deinen Videos dafür, dass aus Ideen Reichweite, aus Zuschauern qualifizierte Leads und aus Personal Brands messbare Ergebnisse werden.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Content-Strategie: Du entwickelst für jeden Kunden einen Content-Plan für die nächsten Wochen und leitest daraus einen klaren Produktionsplan für die Cutter ab.

  • Ideen und Skripte: Du findest die Themen, Hooks und Titel für alle Hauptvideos auf YouTube und schreibst die Skripte selbst.

  • Dreh: Du begleitest Drehs, verstehst Kamera, Licht und Ton und greifst selbst zur Kamera, wenn es nötig ist.

  • Schnitt und Qualität: Du gibst jedes Video frei, bevor es zum Kunden geht. Was nicht gut genug ist, geht zurück.

  • Cutter-Führung: Du führst das Cutter-Team, gibst regelmäßig konkretes Feedback und machst jeden Editor messbar besser.

  • Shortform und Ads: Du sorgst dafür, dass aus jedem Longform-Video verwertbare Clips und Ad-Creatives entstehen.

  • Kundenkommunikation: Du führst die Weeklys mit unseren Kunden, erklärst, was produziert wird und warum, und vertrittst deine Entscheidungen auch dann, wenn der Kunde anders denkt.

Was für dich drin ist:

  • Starkes Team: Familiäres Umfeld, gemeinsame Erfolge und Geburtstage

  • Schnelle Wege: Deine Ideen werden intern umgesetzt, statt in endlosen Entscheidungsschleifen zu versanden

  • Direkter Impact: Deine Videos beeinflussen unmittelbar Reichweite, Leads und Umsätze unserer Kunden

  • Führung: Du führst ein eigenes Cutter-Team und prägst, wie bei uns Content entsteht

  • Wachstum: Du arbeitest mit unterschiedlichen Personal Brands, Formaten und Zielgruppen und entwickelst dich als Creator und Führungskraft kontinuierlich weiter

Das bringst du mit:

  • Nachweisbare Erfahrung als Content Creator, Video Producer oder Head of Content, idealerweise mit Fokus auf YouTube-Longform, Shortform und Video-Ads

  • Ein Portfolio mit Videos, die du verantwortet hast, idealerweise mit messbaren Ergebnissen wie Views, Klickrate und Zuschauerbindung

  • Fundiertes Verständnis dafür, was ein Video viral macht: Hook, Titel, Thumbnail, Storytelling und Retention

  • Starkes Gespür für Ideen und Skripte: Du schreibst YouTube-Skripte selbst, die Zuschauer bis zum Ende halten

  • Editing auf hohem Niveau: Longform, Shortform und cinematic – idealerweise bist du selbst Creator

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Kamera, Licht und Ton: Du kannst selbst drehen

  • Verständnis für Video-Ads und ihre Rolle im Funnel und in der Customer Journey

  • Sicherer Umgang mit relevanten Kennzahlen wie CTR, Zuschauerbindung, Views und CPL

  • Führungserfahrung: Du steuerst mehrere Cutter gleichzeitig, planst Produktion und gibst Feedback, das dein Team besser macht

  • Souveräne Kundenkommunikation: Du führst Weeklys und vertrittst deine Content-Entscheidungen auch gegenüber anspruchsvollen Unternehmern

  • Hohe Standards: Kein Video verlässt dein Team, hinter dem du nicht selbst stehst

  • Eigenverantwortung: Du wartest nicht auf Ansagen, sondern bringst eigene Ideen und Trends ein

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau

  • Ein Plus: Erfahrung mit Podcast- und Event-Drehs sowie tiefes Technik-Verständnis (Kamera-Setups, Equipment, Workflows)

Du passt eher nicht zu uns, wenn …

  • du lieber schöne Bilder produzierst, statt Videos, die Reichweite und Nachfrage erzeugen

  • du nur schneiden willst und Ideen, Skripte und Strategie anderen überlässt

  • du dich auf Bauchgefühl verlässt und Klickrate, Retention und Views ignorierst

  • du Videos rausgibst, hinter denen du selbst nicht stehst

  • du Trends anderer kopierst, statt eigene Ideen und Formate zu entwickeln

  • du Feedback persönlich nimmst oder deinem Team kein klares Feedback geben willst

  • du lange an einem einzelnen Video feilst, aber Schwierigkeiten hast, im Volumen zu liefern

  • du Deadlines eher als Empfehlung siehst

  • du Kunden nicht klar sagen magst, wenn etwas nicht funktioniert

  • dich klare Ziele, Zahlen und ein performanceorientiertes Umfeld eher abschrecken

  • du einfach nur einen Job suchst und nicht bereit bist, dich fachlich und persönlich weiterzuentwickeln


Klingt nach dir? Dann lass uns herausfinden, ob wir zusammenpassen – bewirb dich jetzt!

title: Customer Success Manager
descriptionHtml:
Help bring new technology to live construction sites

 

About XYZ Reality

XYZ Reality created the world’s first engineering-grade augmented reality for construction. Our site-safe hardhat, The Atom, overlays the design model onto the live build, so our engineers can verify work as it goes in on some of the most complex mission-critical projects in the world.

Backed by Series B investment and growing fast across the US, UK and Europe, we’re a driven, passionate team changing how the industry builds.

If you want your work to shape how the world gets built, we’d like to hear from you.

Our project delivery team runs XYZ's service on site across multiple active projects, from mobilisation to handover.

 

THE ROLE

Customer Success Managers are the face of XYZ Reality for our clients. You'll help people feel the product.
This role is for someone who has spent years in construction delivery, in Electrical Engineering, CSA, Project Controls or Commissioning, and knows the industry inside out. You'll use that experience to connect with site teams on their level, understand their pressures, and show them how XYZ Reality helps them deliver better. You're not a software salesperson. You're a construction professional who has found a better way.
You'll spend a lot of time on sites, working directly with project teams and building trust. You'll also hold your own in a room with VPs and senior client stakeholders, translating field reality into business value.

Location: We're open to candidates based in the UK or across Europe, with regular travel to client sites.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the day-to-day client relationship across your assigned projects, acting as the primary point of contact for site teams, project managers, and senior stakeholders to ensure they are getting full value from the XYZ platform.

  • Drive on-site adoption of the XYZ platform, working directly with field teams to embed the service into daily workflows, remove adoption barriers, and ensure the product is genuinely improving how work gets done.

  • Be the bridge between site and senior leadership, translating on-the-ground performance, issues, and wins into clear reporting and insight for client Project Directors, Construction Directors, and VPs.

  • Identify risks to client satisfaction or adoption early, flagging issues proactively, coordinating with internal teams to resolve them, and maintaining a high standard of delivery across every project touchpoint.

  • Support commercial growth, contributing to account retention and expansion by building strong relationships, demonstrating measurable delivery impact, and working with colleagues on client conversations.

  • Feed real-world insight back into XYZ, sharing client feedback, site observations, and adoption patterns with colleagues to help shape how the platform and service evolves.

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Proven background in construction delivery with specialism in one or more of: Electrical Engineering, Civil / Structural / Architectural (CSA), Project Controls, or Commissioning, on major programmes.

title: Customer Success Onboarding Specialist (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Unsere Vision

Wir wollen das beliebteste finanzielle Betriebssystem für KMU (kleine und mittlere Unternehmen) und Steuerberatungsgesellschaften werden.

Wir helfen Unternehmern, sich von zeitraubenden Aufgaben rund um Buchhaltung und Finanzen zu befreien, während wir ihnen gleichzeitig Zugang zu wichtigen Finanzinformationen verschaffen, um die besten Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen zu treffen.

Deine Mission

Du bist die Stimme unserer deutschen Kunden und trägst direkt dazu bei, dass sie mit Pennylane erfolgreich sind. Du hilfst kleinen und mittleren Unternehmen (KMU), ihre Finanzprozesse zu vereinfachen und das volle Potenzial unserer Finanzmanagement-Plattform auszuschöpfen. Gleichzeitig gestaltest du mit uns den Aufbau von Pennylane in Deutschland.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Onboarding mit Wirkung: Du begleitest neue KMU-Kunden und ihre Steuerkanzleien durch den gesamten Onboarding-Prozess. Du sorgst dafür, dass der Einstieg reibungslos gelingt und Unternehmen schnell von den Möglichkeiten unserer Plattform profitieren.
  • Kundenbeziehungen aufbauen und weiterentwickeln: Du bist die erste Ansprechperson für unsere bestehenden KMU-Kunden. Du baust vertrauensvolle Beziehungen auf, erkennst Potenziale für zusätzliche Funktionen und eine erweiterte Nutzung und hilfst deinen Kunden, ihre unternehmerischen und finanziellen Ziele mit Pennylane zu erreichen.
  • Proaktiv beraten: In regelmäßigen Gesprächen prüfst du, wie erfolgreich deine Kunden mit Pennylane arbeiten und wo sie Unterstützung brauchen. Du steigerst ihre Zufriedenheit, optimierst die Nutzung der Plattform und erkennst frühzeitig, wenn eine Abwanderung droht.
  • Gemeinsam den deutschen Markt gestalten: Du arbeitest eng mit unserem deutschen Sales-Team und dem lokalen Leadership-Team zusammen. Gemeinsam entwickelt ihr Abläufe weiter, bündelt Produktfeedback und treibt das Wachstum von Pennylane in Deutschland voran.
  • Expertise aufbauen und teilen: Du entwickelst dich zur gefragten Ansprechperson für unsere Plattform und die deutsche Finanz- und Buchhaltungslandschaft. Dein Wissen und bewährte Vorgehensweisen gibst du direkt an unsere KMU-Kunden weiter.

Das bringst du mit

  • Relevante Erfahrung: Du hast 2–5 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Buchhaltung, im Finanzmanagement, in Corporate Finance oder in einer vergleichbaren unternehmensinternen Rolle. Idealerweise hast du selbst mit Finanzprozessen, Rechnungsstellung oder Buchhaltungsabläufen gearbeitet. Erfahrung im B2B-SaaS-Umfeld, bei einem Fintech oder in einer Steuerkanzlei ist ein Plus.
  • Fachliche Grundlage: Du hast ein Studium mit Schwerpunkt Finanzen, Rechnungswesen oder Betriebswirtschaft abgeschlossen. Alternativ bringst du eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Steuerfachangestellter, eine Weiterbildung als Steuerfachwirt oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation im Rechnungswesen mit.
  • Verständnis für den deutschen Markt: Du kennst die Anforderungen von KMU an ihr Finanzmanagement und verstehst die zentralen Abläufe rund um Rechnungswesen, Rechnungsstellung und das finanzielle Tagesgeschäft in Deutschland.
  • Kommunikationsstärke und Empathie: Du hörst aufmerksam zu, versetzt dich in deine Kunden hinein und erklärst komplexe finanzielle oder technische Themen einfach und verständlich.
  • Lust, selbst anzupacken: Du möchtest Teil eines Teams sein, das in Deutschland noch am Anfang steht und wächst. Du ergreifst die Initiative, denkst in Lösungen und hast Freude daran, Prozesse von Grund auf mitzugestalten.
  • Reisebereitschaft: Du freust dich darauf, unser Team beim Onboarding im Pariser Headquarter kennenzulernen, und bist bereit, gelegentlich Kunden in Deutschland zu besuchen – etwa einmal im Monat.
  • Sprachkenntnisse: Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem oder verhandlungssicherem Niveau (C2) und fließend Englisch für die Zusammenarbeit mit unseren internationalen Teams.

Was wir tun, um dein Arbeitsleben besser zu machen

  • Du kannst remote aus deinem Wohnsitz arbeiten, solange es in Deutschland liegt. Regelmäßige Arbeit aus dem europäischen Ausland ist möglich, wenn die Zeitverschiebung zur MEZ (Mitteleuropäische Zeit) maximal zwei Stunden beträgt.
  • Unabhängig davon, wo du ansässig bist, erhältst du 30 von Pennylane bezahlte Urlaubstage.
  • Du erhältst ein wettbewerbsfähiges Vergütungspaket.
  • Du erhältst Unternehmensanteile, um vom Erfolg mitzuprofitieren, den du gemeinsam mit uns aufbaust.
  • Du erhältst ein Budget, um dein Zuhause in einen komfortableren Arbeitsplatz zu verwandeln, sowie eine monatliche Pauschale, um in einem Coworking Space zu arbeiten, wann immer du möchtest. In Berlin haben wir ein Office, aus dem regelmäßig gearbeitet werden kann.
  • Du erhältst die neueste Apple-Ausrüstung.
  • Wir legen Wert auf regelmäßige gemeinsame Veranstaltungen wie unsere Tech Days (die Remote-Pennylaner alle 3 Monate zusammenbringen) oder unser jährliches Firmenseminar, um wichtige Momente des Zusammenhalts für alle zu schaffen.

Wen wir suchen

Um bei Pennylane erfolgreich zu sein, benötigst du:

  • Englischkenntnisse (das Niveau wird je nach Abteilung, für die du dich bewirbst, bewertet und eingeschätzt).

title: Data Center Operations Implementation Manager
descriptionHtml:
Role Overview

We are seeking a Data Center Operations Implementation Manager to own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition of Nscale's data centres — spanning construction, fit-out, and live, steady-state local operations — across an assigned region and set of sites. Rather than owning construction execution itself, you'll be the connective tissue between Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, and local Operations teams — driving a structured, well-documented transition so every site goes live on schedule and ready to support production workloads. This is an individual-contributor role built on strong stakeholder management, cross-functional influence, and travel to sites during critical transition windows.

What You'll Do

Day 0 to Day 2 Transition Leadership

  • Own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition process for each data centre site within your assigned region — spanning construction, fit-out, and steady-state operations.
  • Define and maintain a standardized transition framework and readiness checklist applied consistently across your assigned sites.
  • Track and drive closure of cross-team action items, dependencies, and blockers standing between construction handover and operational go-live.
  • Identify and escalate risks to go-live timelines, and drive resolution across the relevant stakeholder groups.

Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Track progress and status across Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, Facility Engineering, SDM, and local site Operations teams throughout the transition window.
  • Partner with Construction teams to track handover status, outstanding items, and site readiness milestones.
  • Track Network Engineering's buildout, testing, and cutover activities required for a site to go live.
  • Track hardware intake, rack-and-stack, and deployment scheduling with Compute/Infrastructure Deployment teams to stay aligned with the transition timeline.
  • Coordinate with Facility Engineering on site systems and infrastructure readiness ahead of transition.
  • Engage with the Service Delivery Management (SDM) team to ensure alignment with customer needs, SLAs, security, and facility performance.
  • Take part in regular cross-functional syncs and stakeholder reviews to stay current on transition status.
  • Contribute to a shared sense of ownership and accountability across stakeholder teams, even without formal authority over them.

Local Day Two Operations Readiness

  • Partner with local Operations leads to confirm staffing, training, tooling, and support processes are in place before a site transitions to Day 2 ownership.
  • Create and validate standard operating procedures (SOPs) and operational processes required for local Operations teams to run the site post-handover.
  • Create the operational site tool bill of materials (BOM) required for local Operations teams to maintain the site post-handover.
  • Verify the spare parts bill of materials (BOM) is complete and in place ahead of Day 2 handover.
  • Facilitate structured knowledge transfer and handover documentation from Construction, Network, and Compute teams to local Operations teams.
  • Confirm monitoring, ticketing, and ITSM processes are validated and operating before a site is handed to local Operations.
  • Act as an escalation point for local Operations teams during the early post-handover period to smooth the transition.

Reliability, Safety & Compliance

  • Define and enforce Day 2 readiness criteria that a site must meet before transitioning to local Operations ownership.
  • Facilitate root-cause analysis for transition delays or gaps surfaced during handover, and drive remediation across teams.
  • Ensure health, safety, and environmental requirements are validated and documented as part of readiness sign-off.
  • Support certification and audit readiness (ISO 27001, ISO 22237, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 22301) ahead of go-live.

Vendor & Supplier Coordination

  • Coordinate with construction contractors and colocation providers as needed to close out remaining items affecting the transition timeline.
  • Track vendor commitments and SLAs relevant to the transition window, and escalate delays that put go-live at risk.
  • Coordinate with the Supply Chain team to align hardware intake and staging with the transition schedule.

Monitoring, Reporting & Analytics

  • Track KPIs and KRIs for the Day 0 to Day 2 transition process (time to transition, readiness checklist completion rate, post-handover incident rate, etc.).
  • Build and maintain dashboards that track transition status across your assigned site pipeline for all stakeholder teams.
  • Produce regular reports for senior leadership on transition status, risks, and blockers.
  • Use data-driven insights to identify systemic bottlenecks in the Day 0 to Day 2 process and drive continuous improvement.

About You

Experience & Background

  • 3-8 years of experience in data centre operations, program/project management, or infrastructure deployment at scale.
  • Proven track record coordinating the transition of new sites into live operations across construction, network, compute, and operations functions.
  • Experience operating in a matrixed environment, influencing outcomes without direct authority over every stakeholder team.
  • Demonstrated success managing multiple concurrent site transitions in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.
  • Background in hyperscale, cloud, or HPC data centre environments (preferred).

Technical Knowledge & Expertise

  • Working knowledge of data centre power, cooling, networking, and compute infrastructure, sufficient to coordinate effectively across specialist teams.
  • Familiarity with network deployment and cutover processes, and compute/hardware deployment lifecycles.
  • Knowledge of Layer 1 network infrastructure, including fiber, copper, optics, and transceivers.
  • Familiarity with ITSM tooling, ticketing systems, and monitoring platforms used by local Operations teams.

Influence & Communication

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and align Construction, Network, Compute, and Operations teams without direct authority.
  • Excellent cross-functional communication skills, able to translate technical detail between teams with different priorities and vocabularies.
  • Program management discipline, with the ability to track and drive multiple concurrent workstreams to closure.
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguous, matrixed, fast-moving environments.
  • Bias toward ownership, pragmatism, and delivering results with urgency.

Operational Excellence

  • Rigorous tracking of readiness checklists, risk logs, and action items across many concurrent site transitions within your assigned region.
  • Proven ability to build and refine standardized transition frameworks that scale with business growth.
  • Strong attention to detail in transition documentation and handover packages.
  • Willingness to travel to sites during critical transition windows.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with program management tooling (e.g., Smartsheet, Asana, Jira, monday.com) for tracking multi-workstream transitions.
  • Familiarity with network cutover or compute/hardware deployment processes specifically.
  • Experience with ITSM platforms and ticketing workflows.
  • Experience with Palantir Foundry or similar data platforms for operational analytics.

At Nscale, we are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities.  We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

title: Data Engineering & Analytics Manager
descriptionHtml:
Insurance is a numbers business, and most of those numbers are harder to trust than they look. You would lead the team that defines the numbers Insify runs on, from the event a customer fires on our website to the report a risk carrier audits months later.


About the Role

You would lead our Data & Analytics team of 3-4 engineers end to end: ingestion, the warehouse and its models, the metric layer, and the analysis and reporting built on top of it. It is a small team with a big surface, so there is nowhere to hide and nothing you can't reach.

We are deliberately not splitting data engineering from analytics. At our size the hard problems sit in the handover between the two, and we want one person who enjoys that whole puzzle.

The team serves four groups with genuinely different needs. Growth wants hourly to daily signals and can live with approximately right. Carrier reporting and corporate finance are calendar-locked and need numbers that reconcile and survive an audit months later. Actuarial needs depth and lineage over speed. Prioritising here is arbitration between things that fail in different ways, and the arbitration is yours.

It's a hands-on role. You can open the warehouse and read the models, you review a new data model before it ships, and your team trusts your technical judgement because you still use it. The job is still the team: its own game, its communication, and each person in it. When something slips, hands-on work is the first thing that yields.


What you'll be doing
  • Leading a team of 3-4 data engineers and analysts end to end: what it builds, how it runs in production, and who you hire and grow to get there
  • Running discovery with the teams we serve: understanding what they need from data, and bringing the platform and datasets that enable them
  • Owning the trade-offs between Growth, carrier reporting, finance and actuarial: deciding what the team works on, driving alignment with key partners across other teams, and saying no when the answer is no
  • Making the platform scale: a new country, carrier or product should mean configuration and reused models, and recurring manual work, like carrier reporting and cash reconciliation, should turn into automation
  • Bringing engineering excellence to how the team works: data contracts with product teams, testing in CI, alerts that get resolved, a way to try changes before they hit production
  • Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others

    • What you'll need
  • You've managed or led a data team before, including hiring, feedback and growing people. It doesn't have to be for long, but it has to be real and you have to want more of it
  • Depth on one side of the data stack and working fluency on the other. You still love shipping, you review your team's work, and they trust your judgement on it
  • A track record of shaping what gets built, not only how: you've turned business problems into data priorities, cut scope, and can show the decisions that followed
  • Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your team's boundaries to get to results
  • You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt. Your team gets that from you: you try new tools and ways of working first, and bring the ones that stick

    • Nice to have
  • Experience with reporting that has to reconcile: bordereaux, revenue, cash, ledger
  • Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech
  • Experience working on a product distributed across different country markets
  • Experience with Databricks, dbt and event tracking (Snowplow or similar)

    • Our stack

    Databricks with Unity Catalog, dbt with SQL-based transformation, running on AWS.

    None of this is a hard requirement, and you don't need to know all of our stack. We care more about how you reason about data, systems and teams than which tools you have used. Strong on most of it? Apply.


    How we hire
    Five conversations, each with a clear purpose, and you hear where you stand after every one:
    1. Leadership. We look at your experience with performance management, personal development and building teams.
    2. Data Model Review. You review a change to our warehouse models with two of our engineers.
    3. Data Platform Design. A modelling and platform problem close to what we deal with.
    4. Values Interview. We look at your approach to work, and how it adds to our Values.
    5. Meet the Founder.
    You get the outcome within three days of your last round, with specific feedback either way.
    We offer
  • Competitive compensation. We offer a salary in the range of 85k-110k EUR plus performance-based equity grants
  • Hybrid. 3 days in the office, 2 from home, up to 4 weeks a year from abroad, 25 holiday days
  • Pension. 6% employer contribution
  • Wellbeing budget. €50 net a month via Epassi, from the gym to takeaway, rolls over
  • Learning and coaching. Internal leadership programs and coaching
  • Central Amsterdam office. Shared lunches, dogs, Friday drinks, high-spec MacBook Pro

    • About Insify

    Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

    We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

    Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.

title: Data Science Lead
descriptionHtml:
Data Science Lead | Semiconductor Metrology
Abingdon, UK

Reward and Benefits

  • £70,000 - £85,000 (depending on experience)
  • Annual bonus, 3x salary death in service benefit and private health care BUPA, EMI Share scheme.

If you are a Data Science Lead who enjoys turning measurement data into proof of what is possible, why not join us in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, and build and lead the Data Science team behind advanced semiconductor metrology systems.

We are looking for an ambitious and adaptable Data Science Lead to set up a new Data Science team in our Technology department, reporting to the Technology Director. You will lead a small team, initially a Data Scientist and a Modelling Scientist, and stay hands-on as a working lead data scientist. You will explore and prove new analysis methods, from synthetic data and information-limit studies to modelling, machine learning and AI, to improve the performance of our Metron3D systems and draw more insight from our data.

You will work hand in hand with the Data Analysis team in Engineering: you prove what is possible, they make it robust and shippable. You will also collaborate with R&D, System Design Engineering and Applications Development. We are an AI-first team, and you will set the standard for using AI tools well and safely. If your passion is speed, evidence and finding out what the data can really tell you, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’ll be doing

  • Lead, develop and mentor the Data Science team while staying hands-on, setting priorities and keeping a fast, evidence-based working rhythm
  • Own and deliver the Data Science roadmap: synthetic data, modelling, information-limit studies, algorithm development and data analysis tools
  • Establish the information limit, meaning what is physically extractable given instrument noise, limitations and tip geometry, and use it as the benchmark for every new method
  • Explore, test and benchmark new algorithms (for example PCA, percentile methods and machine learning) on real and synthetic data, covering achievable performance, measurement uncertainty and gauge capability
  • Define the handover to Data Analysis in Engineering (prototype code, test data, acceptance criteria and expected performance), and manage the demo and performance data libraries with Applications Development
  • Use AI tools every day, set the team’s standards for using them well and safely, and track the state of the art in third-party and open-source methods

Education and experience

  • MSc or PhD in Physics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a similar subject, or [8] years’ relevant experience in data science or quantitative research, including some team leadership

Skills and experience we’re looking for:

  • Experience leading or mentoring a team of data scientists, scientists or engineers
  • Hands-on data science in Python (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn or similar), turning exploratory work into quantified results
  • Heavy, day-to-day use of AI tools in your own technical work, such as coding assistants, LLMs and agentic workflows, with a critical eye for checking their outputs
  • Image processing, signal processing or statistical analysis of measurement data from scientific instruments
  • Statistical methods for measurement systems: uncertainty, repeatability, gauge R&R and drift
  • Machine learning and/or physics-based modelling, with the judgement to pick the right tool for the problem
  • Clear communication of results to technical and non-technical audiences, with evidence-based recommendations
  • Comfortable setting a roadmap and priorities, and knowing when a result is good enough to hand over

We’d love to see:

  • Atomic Force Microscopy or other nano-characterisation (SEM, FIB, profilometry), or semiconductor metrology and process control
  • Synthetic data generation or forward modelling of instruments
  • Building AI-assisted workflows or tooling for a team (agents, automated analysis pipelines, shared prompt libraries), and handing prototypes to software teams to productionise

A bit about us: 

Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world. 

Our strength lies in the varied perspectives that come from different cultures, experiences, and identities. We believe that true innovation is fuelled by collaboration, locally and globally. We strive to foster an environment where everyone can contribute meaningfully and thrive. If you require adjustments to take part in the recruitment process, please let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

Your recruitment journey:

We will interview you: Monday to Friday UK Time 9am to 4.30pm and we'll be as flexible as we can with Global Scheduling

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to to know more about us

If you're not comfortable with eye contact, let us know at the start of your interview and if REMOTE, once we've said hello, feel free to turn your camera off until the end.

We dress casually so informal attire is absolutely fine for onsite interviews. We want you to feel comfortable when you meet us and if there's anything else we can do to support your journey, just let us know. 

A note on how we use AI:
We use AI only to transcribe our interviews so we can focus fully on you instead of scribbling notes. The AI does not take part in any decision making at any stage. All hiring decisions are made by real humans based on the conversation we have with you.

Location and working pattern:
We recognise the value of flexibility and offer a hybrid working model wherever possible. Most employees work onsite three days per week, although some positions require a greater onsite presence due to the nature of the work and business need

Recruitment agencies: Infinitesima Ltd only works with approved agencies and does not accept unsolicited agency CVs. Please do not submit candidate details in response to this advert or solicit any Infinitesima Ltd employees. Infinitesima Ltd is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited CVs.

title: Deine studienintegrierte Ausbildung: Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) und Informatik B.Sc.
descriptionHtml:
Studienintegrierende Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration mit Bachelorstudium Informatik (B.Sc.)

Dein Einstieg in die IT: Theorie verstehen, Praxis erleben, Zukunft gestalten.

Du interessierst dich für Informatik, möchtest technische Zusammenhänge verstehen und hast Freude daran, Lösungen für knifflige Aufgaben zu finden? Gleichzeitig möchtest du nicht nur theoretisch lernen, sondern dein Wissen von Anfang an in der Praxis anwenden?

Dann könnte unsere studienintegrierende Ausbildung genau das Richtige für dich sein.

Bei der Deutschen Extrakt Kaffee GmbH (DEK) verbindest du eine Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration mit einem Bachelorstudium der Informatik an der Beruflichen Hochschule Hamburg (BHH).

In Zusammenarbeit mit der BHH bieten wir dir die Möglichkeit, innerhalb von vier Jahren einen anerkannten Berufsabschluss und den akademischen Abschluss Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) zu erwerben.

Dabei lernst du unsere IT-Systeme und digitalen Prozesse kennen, sammelst praktische Erfahrungen und vertiefst gleichzeitig dein theoretisches Wissen.

So verbindest du das Beste aus Ausbildung und Studium und legst eine vielseitige Grundlage für deine berufliche Zukunft.

Das erwartet dich in deiner studienintegrierenden Ausbildung

Bei uns lernst du die IT eines international tätigen Unternehmens kennen und erfährst, wie technische Systeme miteinander verbunden sind und im Arbeitsalltag eingesetzt werden.

Dabei wechselst du zwischen drei Lernorten: unserem Unternehmen, der Berufsschule und der Beruflichen Hochschule Hamburg (BHH).

Das bedeutet für dich:

  • Du lernst unsere IT-Welt kennen: Von Computern und Netzwerken über Server bis hin zu komplexeren IT-Systemen erfährst du, wie unsere technische Infrastruktur aufgebaut ist und zusammenarbeitet.

  • Du verbindest Theorie und Praxis: An der BHH beschäftigst du dich mit den wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen der Informatik, während du dein Wissen bei uns im Unternehmen praktisch anwenden und vertiefen kannst.

  • Du bringst Technik zum Laufen: Du unterstützt bei der Einrichtung, Betreuung und Weiterentwicklung unserer IT-Systeme und lernst, wie wir für einen zuverlässigen IT-Betrieb sorgen.

  • Du gehst Problemen auf den Grund: Du analysierst technische Störungen, suchst nach Ursachen und entwickelst gemeinsam mit deinem Team passende Lösungen.

  • Du beschäftigst dich mit IT-Sicherheit: Du erfährst, wie wir unsere Systeme, Netzwerke und Daten schützen und welche Bedeutung IT-Sicherheit für unser Unternehmen hat.

  • Du gestaltest digitale Lösungen mit: Du lernst unsere IT-Prozesse kennen und kannst dich in Projekte einbringen, mit denen wir unsere technische Infrastruktur und digitale Arbeitsabläufe weiterentwickeln.

  • Du wächst mit deinen Aufgaben: Mit zunehmendem Wissen und Erfahrung übernimmst du eigene Aufgaben und entwickelst dich fachlich und persönlich weiter.

Ausbildung und Studium: So funktioniert das Modell

Mit der studienintegrierenden Ausbildung bieten wir dir gemeinsam mit der Beruflichen Hochschule Hamburg (BHH) einen Bildungsweg, der berufliche Praxis und akademisches Lernen miteinander verbindet.

Das Besondere: Ausbildung und Studium laufen nicht einfach unabhängig voneinander ab, sondern sind inhaltlich und organisatorisch aufeinander abgestimmt.

Während deiner vierjährigen Ausbildungs- und Studienzeit lernst du an drei unterschiedlichen Orten:

  • Bei uns im Unternehmen: Du sammelst praktische Erfahrungen, lernst unsere IT-Abteilung kennen und arbeitest an betrieblichen Aufgaben und Projekten mit.

  • In der Berufsschule: Du erwirbst die beruflichen Fachkenntnisse, die du für deine Ausbildung zum Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration benötigst.

  • An der BHH: Du vertiefst dein Wissen im Bachelorstudiengang Informatik und beschäftigst dich unter anderem mit Programmierung, Mathematik, Softwareentwicklung und IT-Sicherheit.

Die Lernphasen sind aufeinander abgestimmt, sodass du dein Wissen aus den unterschiedlichen Bereichen miteinander verbinden kannst.

Am Ende kannst du gleich zwei Abschlüsse in der Tasche haben: deinen Berufsabschluss als Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration und den Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) in Informatik.

Das bringst du mit

Du möchtest Informatik studieren, gleichzeitig praktische Erfahrungen sammeln und verstehen, wie IT-Lösungen im Unternehmensalltag eingesetzt werden? Dann bringst du schon eine wichtige Voraussetzung mit.

Was uns außerdem wichtig ist:

  • Du hast die (Fach-)Hochschulreife oder stehst kurz vor deinem Abschluss und erfüllst die Zugangsvoraussetzungen der BHH.

  • Du interessierst dich für Informatik, digitale Technologien und technische Zusammenhänge.

  • Du hast Freude daran, logisch zu denken, Zusammenhänge zu erkennen und Lösungen für knifflige Aufgaben zu finden.

  • Du beschäftigst dich gerne mit neuen Themen und bringst die Motivation mit, dich sowohl im Studium als auch in der Praxis weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Du arbeitest gerne mit anderen zusammen, bist offen für neue Ideen und scheust dich nicht, Fragen zu stellen.

  • Du kannst dich gut organisieren und bist bereit, die Anforderungen von Ausbildung und Studium miteinander zu verbinden.

Du musst noch kein IT-Profi sein. Erste Erfahrungen mit Computern oder Programmierung sind natürlich hilfreich, aber viel wichtiger sind uns dein Interesse an Informatik, deine Lernbereitschaft und die Freude daran, Neues auszuprobieren.

Unser Angebot

  • Bei uns kannst du Ausbildung und Privatleben super verbinden! Dank unserer Gleitzeitregelung hast du die Möglichkeit, deinen Arbeitstag flexibel zu gestalten – so lassen sich Familie, Freizeit und Beruf optimal miteinander vereinbaren.

  • Bei uns startest du im ersten Lehrjahr mit 1.284€ brutto. Dies erhöht sich im zweiten Lehrjahr auf 1.342€ brutto und im dritten Lehrjahr auf 1.412€ brutto. Zusätzlich bieten wir Dir Urlaubsgeld, Weihnachtsgeld und jährliche Gehaltsanpassungen.

  • Unsere Idee ist, dass du nach der Ausbildung bei uns bleibst: Du erhältst eine strukturierte Einarbeitung und eine praxisnahe Ausbildung. So hast du die besten Chancen, nach deiner Ausbildung übernommen zu werden und langfristig mit uns gemeinsam zu wachsen.

  • Karriere mit Geschmack: Du erhältst monatliche Freikontingente, damit Du auch nach der Arbeit erstklassigen Kaffee oder Kakao genießen kannst.

  • Unsere Mitarbeitenden liegen uns am Herzen, u.a. mit Geburtstags- und Weihnachtsgeschenken machen wir Dir regelmäßig eine Freude.

  • Wir bieten Dir weitere Benefits wie unsere betriebseigene Kantine, in der täglich frisch gekocht wird, eine Übernahme des Deutschlandtickets, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, vergünstigte Sport- und Gesundheitsangebote über machtfit und ein professionelles Mental Health Angebot durch das Fürstenberg Institut. 

Dürfen wir uns kurz vorstellen?

Familiär. International. Langfristig.

Besondere Qualität entsteht, wenn Tradition und Moderne miteinander harmonieren. 

Wir gehen respektvoll, offen und hilfsbereit miteinander um und geben jeden Tag unser Bestes, um erstklassige Kaffee-Spezialitäten zu produzieren.

Bei der DEK arbeiten Sie in einem internationalen Umfeld und spüren zugleich die Vorteile eines inhabergeführten Familienunternehmens.

descriptionHtml:
Localisation
